_about: Cloud 2026-11-03. IELTS exams 1-6: the Common mistake pair on key point 3 (the trap / language point), written as a mini exam item. Academic explain only (gt:false): the GT Learn pages keep their own trap text.

x01-l1.right: You write 'passport'. The word before the gap is already printed.

x01-l2.wrong: She mentions the bus, so the answer is B (bus).
x01-l2.right: She says 'but the train is quicker', so the answer is C (train).

x01-l3.wrong: 'That's one way of looking at it' = she agrees.
x01-l3.right: 'That's one way of looking at it' = polite disagreement. Listen for what they finally accept.

x01-l4.wrong: You hear 'turning now to costs' and keep filling the 'Benefits' notes.
x01-l4.right: 'Turning now to costs' = next heading. The next answer is under 'Costs'.

x01-r1.wrong: The passage says nothing about the price, so 'It was cheap' is FALSE.
x01-r1.right: No information = NOT GIVEN. FALSE needs the opposite in the text.

x01-r2.wrong: Paragraph C is about funding, so 'a mention of a rejected grant' must be C.
x01-r2.right: Scan every paragraph for the rejected grant itself. A detail can sit in a paragraph about something else.

x01-r3.wrong: The passage quotes a critic who says the plan failed, so YES, the writer thinks it failed.
x01-r3.right: That is the critic's view. Find the writer's own words before you choose YES or NO.

x01-s.wrong: Last year I go to Antalya and I am staying two weeks.
x01-s.right: Last year I went to Antalya and stayed for two weeks.

x01-w2.wrong: I am agree with this statement.
x01-w2.right: I largely agree with this view, although there is one exception.

x02-l1.right: FifTEEN (stress on -teen) = 15; FIFty = 50. Check it against the next number you hear.

x02-l2.wrong: The guide says 'cafe' first, so the cafe is at A.
x02-l2.right: Follow the directions: 'past the cafe, then on your left' puts the cafe before the answer, not at it.

x02-l3.wrong: The student suggests a survey, so the answer is 'survey'.
x02-l3.right: The tutor says 'I'd leave that out'. The answer is what they agree in the end.

x02-l4.wrong: Notes: 'main problem: ___'. You expect 'pollution' and write it.
x02-l4.right: The speaker says 'noise'. Write the word you hear, in the form you hear it.

x02-r1.wrong: The notice doesn't mention weekends, so 'Open at weekends' is FALSE.

x02-r2.wrong: Section B is headed 'Costs', so 'a figure for annual costs' is B.
x02-r2.right: Look for the figure itself. It may appear in a section about something else.

x02-r3.wrong: 'Some economists argue the tax works' - so YES.
x02-r3.right: That is the economists' view. If the writer never says so, it is NOT GIVEN.

x02-s.wrong: Do you like your area? - Yes.
x02-s.right: Yes, mostly. It's quiet, and there's a market every Saturday that I love.

x02-w1.wrong: The car park removed and a garden built.
x02-w1.right: The car park was removed and a garden was built.

x02-w2.wrong: Some people think concerts are better. I think concerts are better.
x02-w2.right: Some people prefer concerts for the atmosphere. In my view, streaming wins on cost and choice.

x03-l1.wrong: He says 'the 9 o'clock boat', so you write 9.
x03-l1.right: He adds 'actually, let's take the 10 o'clock'. The final choice is the answer: 10.

x03-l2.wrong: 'People assume I trained in Italy' - you write Italy.
x03-l2.right: 'In fact I learned everything here in Leeds' - Leeds. The assumption is the trap.

x03-l3.wrong: 'We thought the fabric would shrink' - answer: shrink.
x03-l3.right: 'but it faded instead' - the fact after 'but' is the answer: faded.

x03-l4.right: The speaker says 'insects'. Copy the plural you hear; it has to fit the sentence.

x03-r1.wrong: 'The horse was first bred in Spain.' The passage says Portugal - NOT GIVEN.
x03-r1.right: The text gives the opposite (Portugal) - FALSE.

x03-r2.wrong: 'Bus lanes were introduced in 2010.' The passage says 'after 2010' - TRUE.
x03-r2.right: 'After 2010' is not 'in 2010' - FALSE. Time words decide.

x03-r3.wrong: Ending C makes a grammatical sentence, so it must be right.
x03-r3.right: Two endings can fit the grammar. Choose the one the passage actually says.

x03-s.wrong: The market has fruit, vegetables, fish, clothes, shoes.
x03-s.right: The market smells of fresh bread, and the fish sellers shout their prices all morning.

x03-w1.wrong: First, they collect the sand. Then they dried it.
x03-w1.right: First, the sand is collected. Then it is dried.

x03-w2.wrong: Working for a year has advantages and disadvantages. In conclusion, both are good.
x03-w2.right: The benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks, mainly because of the work experience.

x04-l1.wrong: 'I used to live on Park Road' - address: Park Road.
x04-l1.right: 'Now I'm at 14 Mill Lane' - the current address is the answer.

x04-l2.wrong: 'Many people think the fair is only for students' - you choose 'students'.
x04-l2.right: 'In fact half the visitors are employers' - the correction is the answer.

x04-l3.wrong: The tutor liked the survey, so 'survey' is the student's choice.
x04-l3.right: The question asks what the student decided. She chose the interviews.

x04-l4.wrong: You hear 'you might expect sugar, but the real cause is salt' and write 'sugar'.
x04-l4.right: The expected idea is the distractor. The answer is 'salt'.

x04-r1.wrong: 'Most of the seaweed was burned.' The passage mentions burning - TRUE.
x04-r1.right: 'Some was burned' is not 'most'. Quantity words decide: FALSE.

x04-r2.wrong: The writer explains the critics' argument clearly, so he agrees with it.
x04-r2.right: Explaining a view is not holding it. Look for 'I believe' or 'in my view'.

x04-r3.wrong: The passage is about map errors, so the writer's view is 'maps are unreliable'.
x04-r3.right: Find the sentence where the writer judges, e.g. 'old maps were more honest than today's'.

x04-s.wrong: My grandmother is very determined and strong.
x04-s.right: My grandmother is determined: at 70 she learned to swim so she could join us at the beach.

x04-w1.wrong: The gym was more popular than the pool with 60%.
x04-w1.right: The gym was more popular than the pool: 60% compared with 25%.

x04-w2.wrong: I totally agree, but I also disagree.
x04-w2.right: I agree that school should start later, but not for children under ten.

x05-l1.right: 'It's gone up to 45' - the current price, 45, is the answer.

x05-l2.wrong: He mentions the glass workshop, so B.
x05-l2.right: He says 'but we chose the pottery one', so the answer is C.

x05-l3.wrong: 'We planned to use the app' - answer: app.
x05-l3.right: 'but the app crashed, so we used paper diaries' - the method they used: diaries.

x05-l4.right: 'It was actually road salt' - the correction: salt.

x05-r1.wrong: 'The lizard is found only on one island.' The passage: 'mainly on one island' - TRUE.

x05-r2.wrong: Dr Lee was criticised for the idea, so Dr Lee did not believe it.
x05-r2.right: Being criticised for an idea means it was Dr Lee's idea. Match each view to the person who holds it.

x05-r3.wrong: 'Critics claim tired judges decide badly' - YES, the writer agrees.
x05-r3.right: The writer says 'the evidence is weaker than it looks' - NO.

x05-s.wrong: The show was very good and I liked it so much.
x05-s.right: The show was gripping. I wanted to know what happened to the sister, so I booked the second part.

x05-w1.wrong: In 2000 the city had 1.2 million people. In 2010 it had 1.5 million. In 2020 it had 1.9 million.
x05-w1.right: The population grew steadily, from 1.2 million in 2000 to 1.9 million in 2020.

x05-w2.right: I agree that transport should be free for students, but not for everyone.

x06-l1.wrong: The council gives meals, so you write 'council' under 'meals'.
x06-l1.right: The daughter cooks the meals; the council provides the alarm. Match each item to its giver.

x06-l2.wrong: The role needs 'patience and a car', so you choose 'patience'.
x06-l2.right: Check the box: the answer is the one option the box lists, 'a driving licence'.

x06-l3.wrong: The tutor says 'nice idea' about the chart, so the comment is 'good'.
x06-l3.right: 'Nice idea, but it needs labels' - the comment is 'needs more detail'.

x06-l4.wrong: 'You'd think it was price, but it's the packaging' - write 'price'.

x06-r1.wrong: 'The fish is popular with tourists.' Nothing about tourists - FALSE.

x06-r2.wrong: The summary says 'people delay tasks they enjoy'. The passage has 'delay' and 'enjoy', so TRUE.
x06-r2.right: The passage says people delay tasks they do NOT enjoy. Same words, opposite meaning - FALSE.

x06-r3.wrong: 'Fans fear the referee will lose authority' - the writer says referees have lost authority.
x06-r3.right: A fear is not a fact. The writer's own claim comes later.

x06-s.wrong: I planned to study abroad, but I changed my mind.
x06-s.right: I had planned to study abroad, but after the interview I realised I wanted to stay.

x06-w1.wrong: The green is in the middle and now the green is in the left.
x06-w1.right: The village green, which was in the centre, has been moved to the west of the site.

x06-w2.wrong: There are many reasons and solutions for this problem.
x06-w2.right: The main cause is X. The best solution, in my view, is Y.
